key_insight: D-Gun-sprayed NiCrAlY delivered better hardness and corrosion resistance on Al 6061-T6, while 80Ni20Cr showed lower erosion mass loss under the tested conditions.
engineering_relevance: Coating selection should reflect the dominant damage mode: NiCrAlY for hardness and chloride-corrosion resistance, or 80Ni20Cr for the tested particle-erosion condition.
method: Deposit 80Ni20Cr and NiCrAlY on Al 6061-T6 using detonation-gun spraying.
Characterize microstructure, phases, roughness and hardness using SEM-EDS, XRD, AFM and nanoindentation.
Evaluate corrosion in 3.5 wt% NaCl, wettability and solid-particle erosion.
evidence_signal: NiCrAlY reached 7895.36 MPa hardness versus 780.11 MPa for 80Ni20Cr, with corrosion rates of 0.00567 and 0.01427 mm/year, respectively, compared with 0.5185 mm/year for bare aluminum.
watch_item: Room-temperature corrosion tests and one erosion condition (90° impact, 40 m/s, 5 min) do not establish long-term service life or performance across operating environments.
paper_title: Microstructure and surface performance of detonation gun sprayed 80Ni20Cr and NiCrAlY coatings on Al 6061-T6 substrate for structural applications
